solves.reason: Emotions = unconscious (not deliberate) response; feelings = cognitive (not physical) assignments; the distinction (not similarity) between them.
'much more complicated' (not simple) dynamic; 'most noteworthy' (not trivial) application; 'more concrete' (not abstract) exemplar.
'more easily grasped' (not overlooked); drum 'merely' (not significantly) helps; march 'energetically' (not reluctantly).
negligible contradicts 'most noteworthy application.' ① complicated, ③ assign, ④ concrete all fit context.
lazily contradicts 'march more energetically.' ① unconscious, ② detailed, ③ conflict all fit context.
dramatically contradicts 'merely' — the drum only/just helps, doesn't dramatically help. ① distinction, ② experience, ④ quickly all fit.
'the ____ between emotion and feeling' — distinction is the only word that fits with 'between X and Y.'
'ability to ____ assign, that is, to think about and make a decision' — cognitively matches the cognitive process described.
'the ____ sensation of the drums' — drums produce sound, so auditory (hearing-related) is correct.
'more easily grasped' in context of understanding a concept = understood. seized is physical meaning.
'cognitively assign, that is, to think about and make a decision about' — assign here means attribute/give meaning to.
'auditory sensation' = sensory input through hearing = perception (awareness through senses).
complicated = complex/intricate. Opposite = straightforward (simple/easy). elaborate and intricate are synonyms.
concrete = definite/specific/tangible. Opposite = vague (unclear/indefinite). tangible and specific are near-synonyms.
(A) 'experience set off by sensation' = triggered/유발하다. (B) 'set off early in the morning' = departed/출발하다.
'a practical example of what has been described; a model or pattern' = exemplar. application/dynamic/sensation don't mean 'example.'
'a much more ___ dynamic' needs past participle adjective. complicate → complicated. More + complicated = comparative.
'the ___ (audit) sensation' needs adjective for hearing. audit → auditory. Not audible (that means 'can be heard').
'feelings are ____ we make to those emotions' — first sentence defines feelings as 'the cognitive assignments.'
'grasped when thinking about ____ — ancient war drums.' The dash introduces war drums as that thing = a more concrete exemplar.
